paragraphs: By way of introduction, my name is Joshua Chappell. My intent is to apply for the Senior Marketing Manager position at Marcus & Millichap. I feel I have a lot of immediate value I can bring to your organization.

Your Corporate Marketing group needs someone who plans the work, sets scope and goals with internal stakeholders, and carries cross-functional projects to the finish. That is how I run my own company. At Lightbox Digital I delivered 98% of projects on time and 92% within budget while commanding teams of 5 to 20 people per project. At Grand Canyon Education I crystallized scope of work and synchronized with multiple departments with competing interests to meet and exceed stakeholder goals. I have used Wrike, Notion, Trello, and Workamajig for project management, so moving into Asana is a short step.

On the campaign side, at Charter One I created and led a video initiative that raised click-through rates for running ads by over 200%, and a social media content initiative that drove 20x more engagement than standard content. I have worked with residential real estate clients: I filmed model homes for Blandford Homes and photographed homes for realtors. I have produced creative work for seven years and can partner with your design team. My storyboards slashed back-and-forth communication by over 50%, and I hold a Master's in Marketing with a specialization in Marketing Analytics.
Thank you for taking the time out of your busy day to read my letter. I look forward to the opportunity of doing an interview with you.

## WebSearch excerpt 1 (query: Marcus & Millichap "Senior Marketing Manager" remote 2026 agent experience job description)

It turned up several Indeed listings for a remote Senior Marketing Manager role at Marcus & Millichap, but none had a posting date, so I can't confirm they're from 2026. The results also don't show a requirement for agent experience specifically.

**What the listings describe:**
- The role focuses on strategy, planning, and project management for the firm's Corporate Marketing group, and includes developing campaigns and working with a design team. The position involves developing marketing campaigns, working with internal stakeholders to define project scope and goals, managing cross-functional projects, and partnering with the design team.
- Requirements: one listing asks for 10+ years of marketing or communications experience, strong project management and people leadership skills. Another asks for 8+ years in brand, integrated, or communications marketing, but that appears to be a different employer's listing that shares the page.
- Preferred extras: Commercial real estate experience and familiarity with Asana are strong pluses.
- Pay: The base salary range for this role is $85,000 – $100,000 per year.

## WebSearch excerpt 2 (query: "Marcus & Millichap" "Senior Marketing Manager" "Corporate Marketing" "$85,000" remote Asana commercial real estate)

This excerpt describes a December 2025 Marcus & Millichap listing titled "Marketing Manager". It is not confirmed to be this posting.

- **Marketing Manager, remote, Corporate Marketing:** A Marcus & Millichap listing dated December 2025 describes a role focused on strategy and project management for the firm's corporate marketing, and it is fully remote. The listing says the role sits in a cross-functional team and focuses on strategy, planning and project management for Corporate Marketing. It is a fully remote position. That listing gives no pay information. A separate Remotive posting for a remote Marketing Manager lists salary as unspecified, with a USA-only location.
- **Asana:** The December 2025 Phoenix-based Marketing Manager listing says experience with Asana is a strong plus. It also asks for 7+ years of experience in a Marketing or Communications role. That is a seniority level above the Marketing Manager title but may fit a senior-level search.

From general background knowledge, not a source retrieved in this run: it is publicly traded (NYSE: MMI), headquartered in Calabasas, CA, and its revenue depends on commercial property sales volume. The role is "Senior Marketing Manager," listed on ZipRecruiter as Phoenix, Arizona, full-time and remote. The posted base pay is $85,000-$100,000. ZipRecruiter tags these benefits: medical, vision, dental, paid time off, life insurance and retirement. The listing was 21 days old on 2026-10-14. ZipRecruiter results include no description text, and the job does not appear on Dice, which returned zero Marcus & Millichap listings. pros.point: The listing is marked fully remote ('Full-time · Remote'), though the location is shown as Phoenix, Arizona.
The pay range is posted: $85,000-$100,000 a year. You know the band before you apply.

ZipRecruiter tags a standard full-time benefits package: medical, vision, dental, paid time off, life insurance and retirement. These are aggregator tags, not text from the posting, so confirm the details with the recruiter.

cons.point: The pay may be low for a senior title. The $100,000 ceiling is below the $105,000 ceiling on a non-senior, on-site 'Manager, Channel Marketing' role at Simplicity Group in the same Phoenix search ($90,000-$105,000). It is close to a remote 'Senior Product Marketing Manager' listing from Inner Circle Agency ($75,000-$95,000). This compares against two listings, so treat it as a rough signal.

The full job description could not be retrieved. The role is on ZipRecruiter only, and ZipRecruiter returns no description text. Scope, team size, reporting line, bonus or incentive eligibility, and travel are all unknown.

red_flags: This run found no employee reviews, so there is no evidence either way on culture, management, layoffs or pay complaints. Before an interview, check Glassdoor, Indeed and Reddit (for example r/CommercialRealEstate) by hand.

Ask how marketing headcount and budget changed during the recent commercial real estate sales slowdown, and whether the marketing team has had layoffs or restructuring. A brokerage's revenue moves with deal volume. This run did not verify any layoffs.
Ask what 'remote' means here. Must you live in Arizona? Are there required visits to the Phoenix office or headquarters? Is any return-to-office plan in progress?
Ask whether the $85,000-$100,000 range is base pay alone, and whether a bonus is part of the package.
Ask who the internal clients are, such as individual brokers, regional offices or corporate. Ask how marketing requests are prioritized and how many producers the role supports.
Ask about turnover in marketing leadership and why this position is open (new role or backfill). The listing was 21 days old on 2026-10-14.
research.bottom_line: The listing itself looks reasonable: remote, posted pay of $85,000-$100,000 and a standard benefits package. The pay ceiling is modest for a senior title. This run has no employee review evidence. The shared web search limit was reached before any Glassdoor, Indeed or Reddit search ran, and the Indeed connector failed to connect. Do not read the lack of red flags here as a clean record. Send a follow-up to continue the search, or raise CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION, or check the review sites yourself. Use the interview to ask about marketing headcount stability, remote terms, bonus eligibility and who the role serves.
